- **Clare** & **Eden Valley**: dry, lime-scented Riesling.
- **Coonawarra**: Cabernet on terra rossa.
- **Margaret River**: Cabernet, Chardonnay.
- **Yarra Valley**, **Tasmania**: Pinot, Chardonnay, sparkling.
- **Hunter Valley**: Sémillon.

cards.title: New Zealand
cards.body: A cool maritime country. **Marlborough** Sauvignon Blanc (intense passion fruit and herbs); **Central Otago** and **Martinborough** Pinot Noir; **Hawke's Bay** Bordeaux blends and Syrah from the **Gimblett Gravels**.

cards.q: Coonawarra's famous red soil is called…
cards.explain: Terra rossa is Coonawarra's famous red soil: a thin strip of red clay over limestone, about 15 km long, ideal for Cabernet. The limestone drains well and keeps the vines in balance.

cards.q: Which New Zealand region is the world's most southerly major wine region?
cards.explain: Central Otago is the world's most southerly major wine region. Its continental climate, the only one in New Zealand, makes ripe, intense Pinot Noir, with hot days and very cold nights.

cards.q: Clare Valley is known for sweet, oaky Riesling.
cards.explain: Clare and Eden Valley Rieslings are bone dry, lime-scented and unoaked, and age to toast and kerosene. They are not sweet or oaky, which makes the statement false.

cards.q: Hawke's Bay's Gimblett ___ are stony soils prized for Syrah and Bordeaux blends.
cards.explain: Hawke's Bay's Gimblett Gravels are former riverbed stones that drain well and store heat. They are prized for Syrah and Bordeaux blends, and a protected zone grows only on these stones.

cards.title: The Cape
cards.body:
Mediterranean climate cooled by the **Benguela Current** and the south-easterly **Cape Doctor** wind.

- **Stellenbosch**: Cabernet, Bordeaux blends, Pinotage.
- **Swartland**: old-vine Chenin and Rhône blends.
- **Constantia**, **Elgin**, **Walker Bay**: cool-climate whites and Pinot.
- **Cap Classique**: traditional-method sparkling.

cards.q: What is the 'Cape Doctor'?
cards.explain: The Cape Doctor is the strong south-east wind that blows across the Cape. It cools vineyards and blows away disease, so many Cape vines need little spraying.

cards.q: Which region led South Africa's old-vine Chenin revival?
cards.explain: The Swartland led South Africa's old-vine Chenin revival: dry-farmed bush vines in a hot, dry region, championed by a new wave of winemakers. Some of the vines are over 50 years old.

cards.q: Vin de Constance is a historic sweet wine once loved by Napoleon.
cards.explain: Vin de Constance, a sweet Muscat wine from Constantia since the 1700s, was loved by Napoleon, and was revived in the 1980s. It was once served at the courts of Europe.

cards.q: South African traditional-method sparkling wine is called Cap ___.
cards.explain: South African traditional-method sparkling wine is called Cap Classique. It is usually Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, with lees aging like Champagne, and is often excellent value.

lessons.title: Deep dive: America and the Southern Hemisphere

cards.title: California and the Judgment of Paris
cards.body:
In **1976**, at a blind tasting in Paris, a Napa Cabernet (Stag's Leap Wine Cellars) and Chardonnay (Chateau Montelena) beat top Bordeaux and Burgundy. The New World arrived.

**Napa Valley** is Cabernet country, with sub-AVAs like Oakville, Rutherford and Stags Leap. Cool, foggy **Sonoma Coast**, **Russian River** and **Carneros** suit Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Oregon's **Willamette Valley** rivals Burgundy for Pinot.

cards.title: Chile and Argentina
cards.body:
**Chile**: a long, thin country cooled by the Humboldt current and Andes winds. Phylloxera never arrived, so many vines grow on their own roots. Signature grape: **Carmenère**. Coastal valleys (Casablanca, Leyda) make crisp Sauvignon Blanc.

**Argentina**: **Malbec** from **Mendoza**, at 800–1,500 m, especially the cool **Uco Valley**. It is a desert: the vines drink **snowmelt** from the Andes, led through irrigation channels, and the altitude keeps nights cool. **Torrontés** in Salta, among the highest vineyards on Earth.

cards.title: Australia
cards.body:
- **Barossa** and **McLaren Vale**: rich Shiraz and GSM blends, some vines over 150 years old.
- **Coonawarra**: Cabernet on red *terra rossa*.
- **Clare** and **Eden Valley**: dry, limey Riesling.
- **Hunter Valley**: long-lived Sémillon.
- **Margaret River**: Bordeaux-style Cabernet and Chardonnay.
- **Yarra Valley** and **Tasmania**: cool-climate Pinot and sparkling.

Australia led the world in **screw caps**.

cards.title: New Zealand and South Africa
cards.body:
**New Zealand**: **Marlborough** Sauvignon Blanc (passion fruit, grass) made the country famous; **Central Otago** grows Pinot Noir in the world's southernmost vineyards.

**South Africa**: winemaking since **1659**. **Chenin Blanc** (locally Steen) is its most planted grape; **Pinotage** (Pinot Noir × Cinsault, 1925) its own crossing. Stellenbosch, Swartland and the cool Elgin and Hemel-en-Aarde valleys lead.

cards.q: What happened at the 1976 Judgment of Paris?
options: California wines beat top French wines blind
cards.explain: The 1976 Judgment of Paris put Napa on the world map: Californian wines beat the best of France in a blind tasting judged by French experts. It changed how the world saw New World wine.

cards.q: Which grape is Chile's signature, once confused with Merlot?
cards.explain: Carmenère is Chile's signature grape, long confused with Merlot. It was only identified in Chile in 1994, and it originally came from Bordeaux.

cards.q: Match the region to its star grape
cards.explain: Each New World region found its specialty: Marlborough with Sauvignon Blanc, Barossa with Shiraz, Mendoza with Malbec and Stellenbosch with Cabernet.

cards.q: Pinotage is a crossing of Pinot Noir and Cinsault.
cards.explain: Pinotage was created at Stellenbosch University in 1925 by crossing Pinot Noir with Cinsault. Cinsault was then called Hermitage in South Africa, hence the name.

cards.title: Missions and gold rush
cards.body:
**Spanish missionaries** planted vines in the Americas for sacramental wine: Peru and Mexico in the 1500s, **Chile** in the 1550s, **California**'s missions from **1769** with the humble **Mission** grape.

The **Gold Rush** brought thirsty miners and European immigrants. Then **Prohibition** (1920–1933) closed most wineries; only sacramental and "grape juice" producers survived.

cards.title: Napa's rise
cards.body:
**Robert Mondavi** opened his Oakville winery in **1966**, the first big new winery in Napa since Prohibition, and labeled wines by grape (Cabernet Sauvignon, Fumé Blanc) instead of borrowing French names.

The **1976 Judgment of Paris** put Napa on the map; **Opus One** (1979) joined Mondavi with Mouton Rothschild.

cards.title: South Africa, Australia, New Zealand
cards.body:
**South Africa**: the Dutch planted vines at the Cape in **1655**; **Constantia**'s sweet wine was drunk by Napoleon. Under apartheid, exports were boycotted; since **1994** the Cape has reinvented itself around old-vine Chenin and Swartland.

**Australia**: vines came with the First Fleet in **1788**; **German Lutherans** settled the **Barossa** in the 1840s, and their Shiraz vines survive. **Penfolds Grange** (1951) showed Australia could make icons.

**New Zealand**: Marlborough's first commercial vineyards were planted in **1973**; **Cloudy Bay** (1985) made it a world classic.

cards.title: Chile and Argentina
cards.body:
In the 1850s Chilean landowners imported French vines, including **Carmenère**, just before phylloxera devastated France. Chile stayed phylloxera-free and kept these old vines.

**Argentina** drank its own huge production until the 1990s, when exporters bet on **Malbec** from high **Mendoza** vineyards. Pioneers such as **Nicolás Catena** proved altitude could make world-class wine.

cards.q: When did Robert Mondavi open his Napa winery?
cards.explain: Robert Mondavi opened his Napa winery in 1966, the first major new Napa winery since Prohibition. Mondavi championed labeling wines by grape and building Napa's image.

cards.q: Who planted the Barossa's old Shiraz vines in the 1840s?
cards.explain: Silesian Lutherans settled in the Barossa in the 1840s and planted vines that still produce wine today. Phylloxera never reached the Barossa, so these are some of the oldest vines in the world.

cards.q: Prohibition (1920–1933) closed most American wineries.
cards.explain: Only producers of sacramental wine and grape juice could legally continue; the industry took decades to recover.

cards.title: Cool spots in warm countries
cards.body: New World producers chase cool sites for elegance: **Adelaide Hills** and **Tasmania** in Australia, **Casablanca** and **San Antonio** in Chile, **Sonoma Coast** in California and **Central Otago** in New Zealand.

cards.title: Signature styles
cards.body: **Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc**: passion fruit and cut grass. **Barossa Shiraz**: rich black fruit and chocolate. **Mendoza Malbec**: plum and violet. **Napa Cabernet**: ripe cassis and polished tannin. **Stellenbosch Chenin**: ripe stone fruit and honey.

cards.q: Which region makes intense, passion-fruit Sauvignon Blanc?
cards.explain: Marlborough makes intense, passion-fruit Sauvignon Blanc: bright sun, cool nights and a long season give a pungent style. Cloudy Bay put it on the map in the 1980s.

cards.q: Match the region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region built its fame on one grape: Marlborough for Sauvignon Blanc, Barossa for Shiraz, Mendoza for Malbec, Stellenbosch for Cabernet. Matching them helps in blind tasting.

cards.q: Chile's Casablanca Valley is cooled by the Pacific Ocean.
cards.explain: Chile's Casablanca Valley is cooled by the Pacific Ocean. Morning fog and sea breezes make Casablanca ideal for Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay, and it was planted from the 1980s.

cards.q: Why are Mendoza's vineyards good for Malbec despite the desert?
cards.explain: Vineyards up to 1,500 m give cool nights, and Andes snowmelt provides water. That combination, with intense sun, gives Mendoza's Malbec its deep color and ripe fruit while keeping some freshness.

cards.q: Pinotage is a South African cross of Pinot Noir and ___.
cards.explain: Pinotage is a South African cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, created in 1925. Cinsault was then called Hermitage in South Africa, hence the name Pinotage.

units.title: Grape files
units.summary: Every Level 5 grape on one card: aromas, structure, origin and where it grows.

cards.title: Dolcetto
cards.body:
'Little sweet one', yet dry: soft acidity, grippy tannin, black cherry and bitter almond. Drunk young in Piedmont.

- **Aromas:** black cherry, black plum, liquorice, almond.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium-low acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** Piedmont, Italy.
- **Where it grows:** Dogliani, Piedmont.
- **Food:** antipasti, salumi, pasta.

cards.title: Montepulciano
cards.body:
Deeply colored, plummy and soft: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo. Not to be confused with the Tuscan town of Montepulciano.

- **Aromas:** black cherry, black plum, dried herbs, liquorice.
- **Structure:** medium-high body, medium acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** Abruzzo, Italy.
- **Where it grows:** Abruzzo, Marche.
- **Food:** lamb skewers, pizza, pasta with meat sauce.

cards.title: Aglianico
cards.body:
'The Barolo of the South': very high tannin and acidity, black fruit, smoke and leather. From volcanic soils in Taurasi and Vulture.

- **Aromas:** black cherry, black plum, smoke, leather, black pepper, earth.
- **Structure:** high body, high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Southern Italy (Campania, Basilicata).
- **Where it grows:** Campania, Basilicata.
- **Food:** braised meats, game, aged cheeses.

cards.title: Nero d'Avola
cards.body:
Sicily's star red: ripe black cherry and plum, medium acidity and soft-to-firm tannins.

- **Aromas:** black cherry, black plum, liquorice, sweet spice.
- **Structure:** medium-high body, medium acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** Sicily, Italy.
- **Where it grows:** Sicily.
- **Food:** caponata, grilled meats, pasta alla norma.

cards.title: Corvina
cards.body:
The main grape of Valpolicella and Amarone: sour cherry and almond when fresh, dried cherry and chocolate when dried (appassimento).

- **Aromas:** red cherry, almond, dried herbs, kirsch, raisin, chocolate.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium-high acidity, medium-low tannin.
- **Origin:** Veneto, Italy.
- **Where it grows:** Veneto.
- **Food:** risotto all'amarone, polenta, aged parmigiano.

cards.title: Mourvèdre
cards.body:
Thick-skinned and sun-loving: blackberry, game, leather and herbs, with high tannin. The 'M' in GSM.

- **Aromas:** blackberry, black plum, game, leather, black pepper, garrigue.
- **Structure:** high body, medium acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Spain.
- **Also called:** Monastrell, Mataro.
- **Where it grows:** Provence, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Jumilla, Barossa Valley, McLaren Vale.
- **Food:** game, braised lamb, barbecue.

cards.q: Which grape shows **black cherry, black plum, liquorice**?
cards.explain: 'Little sweet one', yet dry: soft acidity, grippy tannin, black cherry and bitter almond. Drunk young in Piedmont.

cards.q: Which grape shows **black cherry, black plum, dried herbs**?
cards.explain: Deeply colored, plummy and soft: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo. Not to be confused with the Tuscan town of Montepulciano.

cards.q: Which grape shows **black cherry, black plum, smoke**?
cards.explain: 'The Barolo of the South': very high tannin and acidity, black fruit, smoke and leather. From volcanic soils in Taurasi and Vulture.

cards.q: Match each grape to a place where it grows
cards.explain: Each grape is matched with one of its key regions from the cards above.

cards.title: Carignan
cards.body:
High in acidity, tannin and color. Once a bulk grape; old bush vines in Priorat, Languedoc and Chile now make serious wines.

- **Aromas:** red cherry, blackberry, dried herbs, liquorice, earth.
- **Structure:** medium-high body, medium-high acidity, medium-high tannin.
- **Origin:** Aragón, Spain.
- **Also called:** Cariñena, Mazuelo, Samsó.
- **Where it grows:** Languedoc-Roussillon, Priorat, Rioja, Maule, Baalbek.
- **Food:** cassoulet, sausages, stews.

cards.title: Cinsault
cards.body:
Light, fragrant and low in tannin: strawberry and flowers. Important in rosé and as a parent of Pinotage.

- **Aromas:** strawberry, raspberry, red cherry, blossom.
- **Structure:** medium-low body, medium acidity, low tannin.
- **Origin:** Southern France.
- **Where it grows:** Provence, Languedoc-Roussillon, Itata & Bío Bío, Swartland, Bekaa Valley, Baalbek.
- **Food:** mezze, grilled fish, rosé-friendly salads.

cards.title: Touriga Nacional
cards.body:
Portugal's finest black grape: deep, floral and concentrated, with violet, blackberry and firm tannin. A key Port grape.

- **Aromas:** blackberry, black plum, violet, liquorice, dried herbs.
- **Structure:** high body, medium-high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Portugal (Dão & Douro).
- **Where it grows:** Douro, Dão, Alentejo.
- **Food:** roast kid, hard cheese, chocolate (port).

cards.title: Petit Verdot
cards.body:
A late-ripening Bordeaux blending grape: inky color, violet and spice, firm tannins. Used in small amounts for structure.

- **Aromas:** blackberry, violet, sweet spice, dried herbs.
- **Structure:** high body, medium-high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Bordeaux, France.
- **Where it grows:** Bordeaux, Napa Valley.
- **Food:** grilled red meat, hard cheeses.

cards.title: Mencía
cards.body:
Fragrant, fresh and medium-bodied: red cherry, blackberry and herbs from steep slate slopes in Bierzo.

- **Aromas:** red cherry, blackberry, violet, dried herbs, black pepper.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium-high acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** North-west Spain.
- **Also called:** Jaen.
- **Where it grows:** Bierzo, Dão.
- **Food:** roast pork, grilled vegetables, octopus.

cards.title: Blaufränkisch
cards.body:
Austria's serious red: dark cherry, pepper and mineral, with bright acidity and firm tannin.

- **Aromas:** black cherry, blackberry, black pepper, wet stones, dried herbs.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium-high acidity, medium-high tannin.
- **Origin:** Central Europe.
- **Also called:** Lemberger, Kékfrankos.
- **Where it grows:** Mittelburgenland, Leithaberg, Neusiedlersee, Eger, Württemberg.
- **Food:** roast duck, goulash, game.

cards.q: Which grape shows **red cherry, blackberry, dried herbs**?
cards.explain: High in acidity, tannin and color. Once a bulk grape; old bush vines in Priorat, Languedoc and Chile now make serious wines.

cards.q: Which grape shows **strawberry, raspberry, red cherry**?
cards.explain: Light, fragrant and low in tannin: strawberry and flowers. Important in rosé and as a parent of Pinotage.

cards.q: Which grape shows **blackberry, black plum, violet**?
cards.explain: Portugal's finest black grape: deep, floral and concentrated, with violet, blackberry and firm tannin. A key Port grape.

cards.q: Match each grape to a place where it grows
cards.explain: Each grape is matched with one of its key regions from the cards above.

cards.title: Zweigelt
cards.body:
Austria's most planted red: juicy red cherry, soft tannins and fresh acidity.

- **Aromas:** red cherry, raspberry, black pepper.
- **Structure:** medium-low body, medium acidity, medium-low tannin.
- **Origin:** Austria (St. Laurent × Blaufränkisch, 1922).
- **Where it grows:** Neusiedlersee, Carnuntum, Austria.
- **Food:** schnitzel, charcuterie, pizza.

cards.title: Xinomavro
cards.body:
'Acid-black': pale, high in acidity and tannin, with tomato, olive and red fruit. Often compared to Nebbiolo.

- **Aromas:** red cherry, tomato leaf, dried herbs, earth, leather.
- **Structure:** medium body, high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Northern Greece.
- **Where it grows:** Naoussa, Amyndeo.
- **Food:** moussaka, lamb, stuffed tomatoes.

cards.title: Agiorgitiko
cards.body:
'St George's grape': soft, plummy and spicy, from medium to full bodied depending on altitude.

- **Aromas:** red plum, red cherry, sweet spice, nutmeg.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** Nemea, Greece.
- **Where it grows:** Nemea.
- **Food:** souvlaki, tomato-based dishes, lamb.

cards.title: Tannat
cards.body:
As its name suggests, fiercely tannic: black fruit, spice and smoke. Madiran's grape and Uruguay's flagship.

- **Aromas:** blackberry, black plum, liquorice, smoke, sweet spice.
- **Structure:** high body, medium-high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** South West France (Madiran).
- **Where it grows:** South West France.
- **Food:** cassoulet, duck confit, grilled steak.

cards.title: Negroamaro
cards.body:
'Black-bitter': dark plum, earth and a bitter twist, from the heel of Italy (Salice Salentino).

- **Aromas:** black plum, black cherry, earth, dried herbs, liquorice.
- **Structure:** medium-high body, medium acidity, medium tannin.
- **Origin:** Puglia, Italy.
- **Where it grows:** Puglia.
- **Food:** orecchiette with sausage, grilled meats.

cards.title: Baga
cards.body:
High-acid, high-tannin grape of Bairrada, for age-worthy reds and fine traditional-method sparkling wines.

- **Aromas:** red cherry, cranberry, tobacco, smoke, earth.
- **Structure:** medium body, high acidity, high tannin.
- **Origin:** Bairrada, Portugal.
- **Where it grows:** Bairrada.
- **Food:** roast suckling pig (leitão).

cards.q: Which grape shows **red cherry, raspberry, black pepper**?
cards.explain: Austria's most planted red: juicy red cherry, soft tannins and fresh acidity.

cards.q: Which grape shows **red cherry, tomato leaf, dried herbs**?
cards.explain: 'Acid-black': pale, high in acidity and tannin, with tomato, olive and red fruit. Often compared to Nebbiolo.

cards.q: Which grape shows **red plum, red cherry, sweet spice**?
cards.explain: 'St George's grape': soft, plummy and spicy, from medium to full bodied depending on altitude.

cards.q: Match each grape to a place where it grows
cards.explain: Each grape is matched with one of its key regions from the cards above.

cards.title: Meunier
cards.body:
Champagne's third grape: buds late and ripens early, avoiding frost. Adds fruity roundness to young Champagne.

- **Aromas:** red apple, red cherry, strawberry, bread.
- **Structure:** medium-low body, medium-high acidity, low tannin.
- **Origin:** France (a mutation of Pinot Noir).
- **Also called:** Pinot Meunier, Schwarzriesling.
- **Where it grows:** Champagne, Vallée de la Marne.
- **Food:** aperitif, charcuterie, fried chicken.

cards.title: Obaideh
cards.body:
Lebanon's best-known native white grape: soft, round and gently aromatic, often compared to Chardonnay. Used in dry whites and to distil arak.

- **Aromas:** lemon, pear, melon, almond, honeysuckle.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium-low acidity.
- **Origin:** Lebanon.
- **Where it grows:** Mount Lebanon, Bekaa Valley.
- **Food:** fattoush, grilled halloumi, fish with tahini.

cards.title: Merwah
cards.body:
Ancient mountain grape from Mount Lebanon, often linked to Sémillon. Waxy texture, citrus and a light nutty finish; a key white in Château Musar's white.

- **Aromas:** lemon, green apple, honey, hazelnut.
- **Structure:** medium body, medium acidity.
- **Origin:** Lebanon.
- **Where it grows:** Mount Lebanon.
- **Food:** mezze, roast chicken, kibbeh.

cards.q: Which grape shows **red apple, red cherry, strawberry**?
cards.explain: Champagne's third grape: buds late and ripens early, avoiding frost. Adds fruity roundness to young Champagne.

cards.q: Which grape shows **lemon, pear, melon**?
cards.explain: Lebanon's best-known native white grape: soft, round and gently aromatic, often compared to Chardonnay. Used in dry whites and to distil arak.

cards.q: Which grape shows **lemon, green apple, honey**?
cards.explain: Ancient mountain grape from Mount Lebanon, often linked to Sémillon. Waxy texture, citrus and a light nutty finish; a key white in Château Musar's white.

units.title: Appellations: rest of Europe
units.summary: Italy, Iberia, central Europe, Greece and Lebanon, region by region.

cards.title: Trentino-Alto Adige
cards.body:
Alpine valleys with German and Italian heritage: pure, aromatic whites and Trentodoc sparkling wines.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Pinot Grigio, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay.

cards.title: Friuli
cards.body:
North-east corner bordering Slovenia: Italy's finest whites, and pioneering skin-contact orange wines.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Glera.

cards.title: Lombardy
cards.body:
Home to Franciacorta, Italy's top traditional-method sparkling wine, and to Alpine Nebbiolo in Valtellina.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Nebbiolo.

cards.title: Emilia-Romagna
cards.body:
Food heaven (Parma ham, Parmigiano) and home of fizzy red Lambrusco.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Sangiovese, Trebbiano.

cards.title: Umbria
cards.body:
Green heart of Italy: Orvieto whites and the tannic Sagrantino di Montefalco.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Sangiovese, Trebbiano.

cards.title: Marche
cards.body:
Adriatic hills: crisp Verdicchio and Montepulciano-based Rosso Conero.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Verdicchio, Montepulciano.

cards.title: Abruzzo
cards.body:
Mountains and sea: soft, plummy Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and Cerasuolo rosé.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Montepulciano, Trebbiano.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Trentino-Alto Adige**?
cards.explain: Trentino-Alto Adige: Alpine valleys with German and Italian heritage: pure, aromatic whites and Trentodoc sparkling wines.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Friuli**?
cards.explain: Friuli: North-east corner bordering Slovenia: Italy's finest whites, and pioneering skin-contact orange wines.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Campania
cards.body:
Volcanic soils around Vesuvius and Avellino: Taurasi (Aglianico), Fiano di Avellino and Greco di Tufo.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Aglianico, Fiano, Greco.

cards.title: Puglia
cards.body:
The hot, flat heel of Italy: ripe Primitivo and Negroamaro.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Zinfandel, Negroamaro.

cards.title: Basilicata
cards.body:
Aglianico del Vulture, grown on the slopes of an extinct volcano.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Aglianico.

cards.title: Sicily
cards.body:
Sunny island making ripe Nero d'Avola, elegant wines from the volcanic slopes of Mount Etna, and fortified Marsala.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Nero d'Avola, Fiano.

cards.title: Sardinia
cards.body:
Island of Cannonau (Grenache) and Vermentino di Gallura.

- **Where:** Italy.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Vermentino, Carignan.

cards.title: Roero
cards.body:
North of the Tanaro river: sandy soils give lighter, fragrant Nebbiolo and white Arneis.

- **Where:** Piedmont, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Nebbiolo.

cards.title: Dogliani
cards.body:
The home of serious Dolcetto.

- **Where:** Piedmont, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Dolcetto.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Campania**?
cards.explain: Campania: Volcanic soils around Vesuvius and Avellino: Taurasi (Aglianico), Fiano di Avellino and Greco di Tufo.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Puglia**?
cards.explain: Puglia: The hot, flat heel of Italy: ripe Primitivo and Negroamaro.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Barbera d'Asti
cards.body:
Juicy, high-acid, low-tannin Barbera around Asti, from everyday to oak-aged Nizza.

- **Where:** Piedmont, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Barbera.

cards.title: Gavi
cards.body:
Crisp, lemony whites from the Cortese grape.

- **Where:** Piedmont, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Cortese.

cards.title: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano
cards.body:
Sangiovese (here called Prugnolo Gentile) from the hill town of Montepulciano. Not to be confused with the Montepulciano grape.

- **Where:** Tuscany, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Sangiovese.

cards.title: Bolgheri
cards.body:
Coastal home of Super Tuscans: Bordeaux varieties such as Sassicaia, Ornellaia and Masseto.

- **Where:** Tuscany, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc.

cards.title: Maremma
cards.body:
Warm southern coast: ripe Morellino di Scansano (Sangiovese) and Vermentino.

- **Where:** Tuscany, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Sangiovese, Vermentino.

cards.title: Carmignano
cards.body:
Historically blended Cabernet with Sangiovese long before the Super Tuscans.

- **Where:** Tuscany, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Sangiovese, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.title: San Gimignano
cards.body:
The town of towers, known for Vernaccia di San Gimignano, a crisp, almondy white.

- **Where:** Tuscany, Italy.
- **Grapes:** Trebbiano.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Barbera d'Asti**?
cards.explain: Barbera d'Asti: Juicy, high-acid, low-tannin Barbera around Asti, from everyday to oak-aged Nizza.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Gavi**?
cards.explain: Gavi: Crisp, lemony whites from the Cortese grape.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Priorat
cards.body:
Steep slopes of llicorella slate: intense, mineral Garnacha and Cariñena from old, low-yielding vines.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Carignan.

cards.title: Rueda
cards.body:
High plateau whites from Verdejo: fresh, herbal and citrusy.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Verdejo.

cards.title: Toro
cards.body:
Hot and dry: powerful, ripe Tinta de Toro (Tempranillo).

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Bierzo
cards.body:
Fragrant Mencía from slate slopes in Castilla y León's green north-west.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mencía.

cards.title: Navarra
cards.body:
Rioja's neighbor, known for Garnacha rosado and modern reds.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Tempranillo.

cards.title: La Mancha
cards.body:
Vast, hot, flat plateau: Spain's largest DO, for value wines (Airén, Tempranillo).

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Jumilla
cards.body:
Hot inland south-east: ripe, dark Monastrell.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mourvèdre.

cards.title: Valdeorras
cards.body:
Galicia's inland river valley on the Sil, and the home of Godello: crisp, mineral whites from slate hills.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Climate:** Cool-continental with Atlantic influence; steep slate slopes.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Priorat**?
cards.explain: Priorat: Steep slopes of llicorella slate: intense, mineral Garnacha and Cariñena from old, low-yielding vines.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Rueda**?
cards.explain: Rueda: High plateau whites from Verdejo: fresh, herbal and citrusy.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Ribeiro
cards.body:
Galicia's oldest wine area: floral, fresh whites from Treixadura and friends in the Miño valley.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Albariño.
- **Climate:** Atlantic with warmer, drier summers than Rías Baixas.

cards.title: Ribeira Sacra
cards.body:
Vineyards on extreme river terraces above the Miño and Sil canyons, farmed by hand. Light, perfumed Mencía reds.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mencía.
- **Climate:** Cool Atlantic climate softened in the sheltered canyons.

cards.title: Monterrei
cards.body:
A warm, sheltered valley in southern Galicia near the Portuguese border: Godello whites and Mencía reds.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mencía.

cards.title: Cangas
cards.body:
A tiny, remote area in the mountains of Asturias where old Albarín and Carrasquín vines grow on steep slopes.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Bizkaiko Txakolina
cards.body:
The Basque coast's Biscay txakoli: very dry, high-acid, lightly sparkling whites, poured from a height.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Climate:** Wet and mild Atlantic, with sea breezes.

cards.title: Getariako Txakolina
cards.body:
Spain's best-known txakoli, from vines on steep slopes above the sea near Getaria. Crisp, saline whites.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Arabako Txakolina
cards.body:
Txakoli from Álava, the inland, slightly warmer of the three Basque txakoli zones.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Cariñena
cards.body:
One of Aragón's oldest DOs, famed for Garnacha and Mazuela (the grape named after the town that gave Carignan its name).

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Tempranillo, Carignan.
- **Climate:** Dry continental with hot summers and cold nights.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Ribeiro**?
cards.explain: Ribeiro: Galicia's oldest wine area: floral, fresh whites from Treixadura and friends in the Miño valley.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Ribeira Sacra**?
cards.explain: Ribeira Sacra: Vineyards on extreme river terraces above the Miño and Sil canyons, farmed by hand. Light, perfumed Mencía reds.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Campo de Borja
cards.body:
The 'Empire of Garnacha' in Aragón: rich, fruity, spicy old-vine Grenache.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Tempranillo.
- **Climate:** Dry, windy (the cierzo) and continental.

cards.title: Calatayud
cards.body:
High-altitude old-vine Garnacha in Aragón, some of the oldest and cheapest great vines in Spain.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Tempranillo, Macabeo.
- **Climate:** Hot days and cool nights; 500 to 1,000 m altitude.

cards.title: Somontano
cards.body:
'Under the mountain': a Pyrenean foothills DO that experiments with international varieties alongside Moristel and Parraleta.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer.

cards.title: Montsant
cards.body:
A horseshoe around Priorat: more affordable Garnacha and Cariñena with its own mineral edge.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Carignan.

cards.title: Terra Alta
cards.body:
The home of Garnacha Blanca in Catalonia: fresh, textured whites and sturdy reds at altitude.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache.

cards.title: Empordà
cards.body:
Catalonia's northeast corner by the French border: windswept Garnacha and Cariñena and sweet 'Garnatxa'.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Carignan.
- **Climate:** Windy Tramontana and Mediterranean warmth.

cards.title: Costers del Segre
cards.body:
A DO in four scattered sub-zones in western Catalonia, including the 'Raimat' estate, with international and local varieties.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay.

cards.title: Conca de Barberà
cards.body:
The cool Catalan basin where Trepat grows, source of much of the base wine for Cava.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Macabeo.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Campo de Borja**?
cards.explain: Campo de Borja: The 'Empire of Garnacha' in Aragón: rich, fruity, spicy old-vine Grenache.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Calatayud**?
cards.explain: Calatayud: High-altitude old-vine Garnacha in Aragón, some of the oldest and cheapest great vines in Spain.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Tarragona
cards.body:
A Mediterranean DO around the Roman city: fruity reds and whites, and the sweet wine tradition of Tarragona.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Carignan, Macabeo.

cards.title: Pla de Bages
cards.body:
A small Catalan DO near Manresa, an hour from Barcelona, with Picapoll as its white speciality.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Macabeo, Chardonnay.

cards.title: Alella
cards.body:
Barcelona's own wine area, on granite 'sauló' sand slopes between the city and the sea; known for Pansa Blanca whites.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache.

cards.title: Cigales
cards.body:
A Castilian DO known for deeply coloured, fruity rosados from Tempranillo and Garnacha.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Grenache.
- **Climate:** Continental with big temperature swings.

cards.title: Tierra de León
cards.body:
A small DO in León with the local Prieto Picudo (reds, rosés) and Albarín Blanco.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Arlanza
cards.body:
A young, high DO on the Arlanza river in Burgos: structured Tempranillo reds and rosados.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Tierra del Vino de Zamora
cards.body:
A small area around Zamora with some of Spain's oldest Tempranillo vines.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Valles de Benavente
cards.body:
A tiny DO in Zamora known for Prieto Picudo and Malvasía.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Tarragona**?
cards.explain: Tarragona: A Mediterranean DO around the Roman city: fruity reds and whites, and the sweet wine tradition of Tarragona.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Pla de Bages**?
cards.explain: Pla de Bages: A small Catalan DO near Manresa, an hour from Barcelona, with Picapoll as its white speciality.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Arribes
cards.body:
Granite-terraced vineyards on the Douro gorge border with Portugal: Juan García and Bruñal, rare native reds.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Sierra de Salamanca
cards.body:
High, rocky vineyards in the Sierra de Francia with Rufete and Garnacha.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache.

cards.title: Cebreros
cards.body:
A small Gredos mountain DO in Ávila: old Garnacha vines on granite at 700 to 1,000 m, a fashionable source of fresh reds.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache.
- **Climate:** High, cool, continental with granite soils.

cards.title: Méntrida
cards.body:
A DO south-west of Madrid with Garnacha vines on granite and slate, now seeing a quality revival.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Syrah.

cards.title: Vinos de Madrid
cards.body:
Three subzones around Madrid: San Martín de Valdeiglesias (Garnacha), Navalcarnero and Arganda.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Grenache, Tempranillo.

cards.title: Mondéjar
cards.body:
A small Castilla-La Mancha area east of Madrid on the Tagus river, growing Cencibel (Tempranillo).

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Uclés
cards.body:
A high-altitude DO in Cuenca for Tempranillo, Garnacha and Syrah.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Syrah.

cards.title: Valdepeñas
cards.body:
A DO inside La Mancha, once famous for light 'clarete' blends of Airén and Cencibel; now known for good-value Tempranillo.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Sierra de Salamanca**?
cards.explain: Sierra de Salamanca: High, rocky vineyards in the Sierra de Francia with Rufete and Garnacha.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Manchuela
cards.body:
High plateau east of La Mancha with Bobal and Garnacha Tintorera, producing darker, serious reds.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Almansa
cards.body:
A high-altitude DO between Albacete and Valencia: dark Garnacha Tintorera and Monastrell.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mourvèdre.

cards.title: Ribera del Júcar
cards.body:
A Cuenca DO along the Júcar river, producing Tempranillo and Bobal.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.title: Utiel-Requena
cards.body:
Valencia's inland plateau, the home of Bobal: dark, juicy reds and rosés and Cava.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Climate:** Continental at 600 to 900 m.

cards.title: Alicante
cards.body:
A warm DO on the Costa Blanca making Monastrell reds and Moscatel, plus the old sweet Fondillón.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mourvèdre, Muscat.

cards.title: Yecla
cards.body:
A high-altitude Monastrell DO in Murcia with limestone soils and dry, sunny weather.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mourvèdre.

cards.title: Bullas
cards.body:
A small DO in Murcia with Monastrell vines at 400 to 800 m, with pure fruit and structure.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Mourvèdre, Tempranillo.

cards.title: Ribera del Guadiana
cards.body:
Extremadura's DO: hot, dry vineyards making Tempranillo reds and Cayetana and Pardina whites.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Manchuela**?
cards.explain: Manchuela: High plateau east of La Mancha with Bobal and Garnacha Tintorera, producing darker, serious reds.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Almansa**?
cards.explain: Almansa: A high-altitude DO between Albacete and Valencia: dark Garnacha Tintorera and Monastrell.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Montilla-Moriles
cards.body:
Córdoba's sherry-style region: fino-like wines and rich Pedro Ximénez without fortification, from a very hot, chalky area.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Pedro Ximénez.
- **Climate:** Very hot continental (summer up to 45 C).

cards.title: Málaga
cards.body:
Sweet wines of Málaga from Moscatel and Pedro Ximénez, plus a fresh range of dry whites and reds from nearby hills.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Muscat, Pedro Ximénez.
- **Climate:** Mediterranean, with mountain-cooled vineyards.

cards.title: Granada
cards.body:
A wide Andalusian DO of vineyards at 1,000 to 1,500 m in the Sierra Nevada foothills, with Tempranillo and Syrah.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Syrah.

cards.title: Condado de Huelva
cards.body:
A south-west Andalusian DO near Doñana making fortified wines and young Zalema whites.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Palomino.

cards.title: Lebrija
cards.body:
A small Cádiz-province DO known for its Moscatel and sweet white wines near Jerez.

- **Where:** Spain.
- **Grapes:** Muscat.

cards.title: Binissalem
cards.body:
Mallorca's historic wine area, with Manto Negro reds on red clay and limestone.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.title: Pla i Llevant
cards.body:
A DO in central and eastern Mallorca with Callet and Manto Negro, and international varieties.

- **Where:** Spain.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Montilla-Moriles**?
cards.explain: Montilla-Moriles: Córdoba's sherry-style region: fino-like wines and rich Pedro Ximénez without fortification, from a very hot, chalky area.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Málaga**?
cards.explain: Málaga: Sweet wines of Málaga from Moscatel and Pedro Ximénez, plus a fresh range of dry whites and reds from nearby hills.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Dão
cards.body:
Granite plateau ringed by mountains: elegant reds and Encruzado whites.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Touriga Nacional, Mencía.

cards.title: Bairrada
cards.body:
Near the coast: tannic Baga reds and traditional-method sparkling wines.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Baga.

cards.title: Lisboa
cards.body:
Atlantic-cooled region north of Lisbon producing fresh, good-value blends.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Touriga Nacional.

cards.title: Tejo
cards.body:
Fertile Tagus river plains making easy-drinking reds and whites.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Touriga Nacional.

cards.title: Setúbal
cards.body:
Peninsula south of Lisbon, famous for fortified Moscatel de Setúbal.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Muscat.

cards.title: Alentejo
cards.body:
Hot, rolling plains (and cork forests): ripe, generous reds. Some wines still made in clay talhas.

- **Where:** Portugal.
- **Grapes:** Tempranillo, Touriga Nacional.

cards.title: Lafões
cards.body:
A small inland Vinho Verde-like region south of the Douro, with high-acid whites and reds.

- **Where:** Portugal.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Dão**?
cards.explain: Dão: Granite plateau ringed by mountains: elegant reds and Encruzado whites.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Bairrada**?
cards.explain: Bairrada: Near the coast: tannic Baga reds and traditional-method sparkling wines.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Rheinhessen
cards.body:
Germany's largest region, once known for bulk Liebfraumilch, now for a new generation of dry wines.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Riesling, Silvaner.

cards.title: Pfalz
cards.body:
Warm and sunny below the Haardt mountains: ripe, full dry Riesling and Pinots.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Riesling, Pinot Noir, Pinot Grigio.

cards.title: Nahe
cards.body:
Varied volcanic and slate soils: precise, mineral Riesling.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Riesling.

cards.title: Ahr
cards.body:
A small northern valley famous for red Spätburgunder.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Pinot Noir.

cards.title: Mittelrhein
cards.body:
The romantic castle-lined gorge of the Rhine: steep slate Riesling.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Riesling.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Rheinhessen**?
cards.explain: Rheinhessen: Germany's largest region, once known for bulk Liebfraumilch, now for a new generation of dry wines.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Pfalz**?
cards.explain: Pfalz: Warm and sunny below the Haardt mountains: ripe, full dry Riesling and Pinots.

cards.title: Franken
cards.body:
Dry, earthy Silvaner in the flat, round Bocksbeutel bottle.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Silvaner, Riesling.

cards.title: Baden
cards.body:
Germany's warmest, southernmost region: Pinot Noir, Grauburgunder and Weissburgunder.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Pinot Noir, Pinot Grigio, Pinot Blanc.

cards.title: Württemberg
cards.body:
Red-wine country around Stuttgart: Trollinger and Lemberger.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch, Riesling.

cards.title: Saale-Unstrut
cards.body:
One of Europe's most northerly quality regions, in former East Germany.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Silvaner.

cards.title: Sachsen
cards.body:
Tiny region around Dresden along the Elbe.

- **Where:** Germany.
- **Grapes:** Riesling.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Franken**?
cards.explain: Franken: Dry, earthy Silvaner in the flat, round Bocksbeutel bottle.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Baden**?
cards.explain: Baden: Germany's warmest, southernmost region: Pinot Noir, Grauburgunder and Weissburgunder.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Kremstal
cards.body:
Around the town of Krems, next to the Wachau: Grüner and Riesling on loess and rock.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Grüner Veltliner, Riesling.

cards.title: Kamptal
cards.body:
Along the Kamp river; the Heiligenstein vineyard is famous for Riesling.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Grüner Veltliner, Riesling.

cards.title: Wagram
cards.body:
Deep loess terraces, rich Grüner Veltliner and Roter Veltliner.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Grüner Veltliner.

cards.title: Weinviertel
cards.body:
Austria's largest region, the 'wine quarter': peppery Grüner Veltliner.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Grüner Veltliner.

cards.title: Carnuntum
cards.body:
Roman-era region east of Vienna making juicy reds.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Kremstal**?
cards.explain: Kremstal: Around the town of Krems, next to the Wachau: Grüner and Riesling on loess and rock.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Kamptal**?
cards.explain: Kamptal: Along the Kamp river; the Heiligenstein vineyard is famous for Riesling.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Thermenregion
cards.body:
Spa-town region south of Vienna with local whites and Pinot Noir.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Pinot Noir.

cards.title: Neusiedlersee
cards.body:
Around Lake Neusiedl: juicy Zweigelt and world-class botrytized sweet wines (Ausbruch, TBA).

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch, Chardonnay.
- **Climate:** The shallow lake creates humid mists that encourage noble rot.

cards.title: Leithaberg
cards.body:
Limestone and schist hills west of the lake: mineral Blaufränkisch and Chardonnay.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch, Chardonnay.

cards.title: Mittelburgenland
cards.body:
'Blaufränkischland': structured, peppery Blaufränkisch.

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch.

cards.title: Steiermark (Styria)
cards.body:
Steep green hills in the south: vibrant Sauvignon Blanc and Morillon (Chardonnay).

- **Where:** Austria.
- **Grapes:** Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Thermenregion**?
cards.explain: Thermenregion: Spa-town region south of Vienna with local whites and Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Neusiedlersee**?
cards.explain: Neusiedlersee: Around Lake Neusiedl: juicy Zweigelt and world-class botrytized sweet wines (Ausbruch, TBA).

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Hungary
cards.body:
Home of Tokaji, the 'wine of kings, king of wines', plus red Bull's Blood (Egri Bikavér) and wines from around Lake Balaton.

- **Grapes:** Furmint, Blaufränkisch.
- **Climate:** Continental, with hot summers and long autumns.

cards.title: Eger
cards.body:
Known for Egri Bikavér, 'Bull's Blood', a Kékfrankos-based red blend.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch.

cards.title: Villány
cards.body:
Hungary's warm south: ripe Bordeaux-style reds.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Cabernet Franc, Merlot.

cards.title: Szekszárd
cards.body:
Loess hills making Bikavér-style blends and Kadarka.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch.

cards.title: Balaton
cards.body:
Volcanic hills around Central Europe's largest lake: aromatic whites.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Furmint.

cards.title: Somló
cards.body:
A single extinct volcano with intense, smoky whites.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Furmint.

cards.title: Kunság
cards.body:
Great Plain sands: Hungary's largest region for everyday wines.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Blaufränkisch.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Eger**?
cards.explain: Eger: Known for Egri Bikavér, 'Bull's Blood', a Kékfrankos-based red blend.

cards.q: Which grape is most associated with **Villány**?
cards.explain: Villány: Hungary's warm south: ripe Bordeaux-style reds.

cards.q: Match each region to its signature grape
cards.explain: Each region is matched with a grape it is known for, as in the cards above.

cards.title: Sopron
cards.body:
Hungary's western corner by the Austrian border: Kékfrankos (Blaufränkisch) reds with a cool, Lake Neusiedl influence.

- **Where:** Hungary.

cards.title: Mátra
cards.body:
Volcanic hills in northern Hungary: fresh whites and Bordeaux-style reds.

- **Where:** Hungary.

cards.title: Etyek-Buda
cards.body:
A cool region west of Budapest known for sparkling base wines, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.

- **Where:** Hungary.
- **Grapes:** Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.title: Balatonboglár
cards.body:
The sunny south shore of Lake Balaton: warm, fruity whites and reds on volcanic and sandy soils.

cards.title: Lebanon
cards.body:
One of the oldest wine cultures on earth, from Phoenician traders to the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek. Today it is known for structured red blends from the high Bekaa Valley.

- **Grapes:** Cinsault, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Carignan, Obaideh.
- **Climate:** Mediterranean, but the vineyards sit high: the Bekaa Valley floor is around 1,000 m, giving hot days, cold nights and a long, dry growing season.
- **Quality system:** No formal appellation system yet; wines are labeled by producer, region and grape.
- Château Musar (founded 1930) made Lebanon famous, with long-lived reds released years after the vintage.
- Château Ksara, founded by Jesuits in 1857, keeps its wine in Roman-era limestone caves.

cards.title: Bekaa Valley

- **Where:** Lebanon.
- **Grapes:** Cabernet Sauvignon, Cinsault, Syrah.
- **Climate:** High plateau (about 1,000 m): sunny, dry summers with cool nights.

- **Grapes:** Cinsault, Carignan.

cards.title: Methoxypyrazines
cards.body: Compounds that give green pepper and grassy aromas.

cards.title: TDN
cards.body: The compound behind the petrol note in aged Riesling.

cards.title: Rotundone
cards.body: The compound responsible for black pepper aromas in Syrah and Grüner Veltliner.

cards.title: LBV
cards.body: Late Bottled Vintage Port: single-year Port aged 4–6 years in wood before bottling.

cards.title: Vintage Port
cards.body: Port from a declared exceptional year, bottled young to age for decades.

cards.title: Aszú
cards.body: Botrytized grapes used to make sweet Tokaji in Hungary.

cards.title: Passito
